title: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates.
authors: Yasuda, Ikki; Yamamoto, Eiji; Yasuoka, Kenji; Lindorff-Larsen, Kresten
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
one_liner_zh: 该文用粗粒化分子动力学模拟研究MED1和FUS凝聚体中客户蛋白的选择性分配，虽非TF-DNA体系，但涉及蛋白-核酸（RNA）互作与序列预测，方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模。
abstract: Biomolecular condensates selectively recruit and exclude proteins, and this partitioning is sometimes dictated by their intrinsically disordered regions. Factors that determine partitioning include client-scaffold interactions and stabilization of the scaffold network within the condensate, yet a molecular and predictive understanding has not been fully achieved. Here, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate molecular interactions between two types of nuclear proteins as scaffolds: the charge-rich disordered region of Mediator 1 (MED1) and the aromatic-rich disordered region of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS), in mixtures with client intrinsically disordered regions from six different proteins. We show distinct partitioning into the MED1 and FUS condensates, while the presence of RNA in both dilute and dense phases modulated client partitioning. Favorable client-scaffold interaction energies within condensates were associated with client partitioning, while client-scaffold interactions competed with scaffold self-interactions. Analysis of interaction energies of individual residues revealed that the interactions were localized to specific sequence regions: charged blocks for interactions with MED1, and dispersed aromatic residues for interactions with FUS. Using residue-resolved interaction energies from our molecular dynamics simulations, we developed sequence-based predictors of client partitioning into MED1 and FUS condensates. Our prediction approach for partitioning can be extended to other biomolecules, offering a framework to analyze their partitioning in cellular environments.
abstract_zh: 生物分子凝聚体选择性地招募和排除蛋白质，而这种分配有时由其内在无序区域决定。决定分配的因素包括客户-支架相互作用以及凝聚体内支架网络的稳定化，然而，分子层面和预测性的理解尚未完全实现。在此，我们使用粗粒化分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟来阐明两种核蛋白作为支架之间的分子相互作用：Mediator 1 (MED1) 的电荷富集无序区域和肉瘤融合蛋白 (FUS) 的芳香族富集无序区域，在与来自六种不同蛋白质的客户内在无序区域混合的情况下。我们展示了在MED1和FUS凝聚体中的不同分配，而RNA在稀相和浓相中的存在调节了客户分配。凝聚体内有利的客户-支架相互作用能与客户分配相关，而客户-支架相互作用与支架自相互作用竞争。对单个残基相互作用能的分析揭示，这些相互作用定位于特定序列区域：与MED1相互作用的带电块，以及与FUS相互作用的分散芳香族残基。利用我们分子动力学模拟中的残基分辨相互作用能，我们开发了基于序列的预测器，用于预测客户在MED1和FUS凝聚体中的分配。我们的分配预测方法可扩展到其他生物分子，为分析其在细胞环境中的分配提供了一个框架。
